title: When the Vow Turns
premise: Mirabel Eriksen built a quiet, careful life around her daughter and the bookshop she inherited, sealing away the heartbreak of the summer her fiancé, Jonah Vale, left to chase a career abroad. When a water-damaged letter — the one he wrote her eleven years ago and never knew she never received — surfaces during a flood in the shop's basement, Jonah returns to town to settle his late mother's estate, and the two are thrown together by the letter's revelations. As they retrace the misunderstanding that broke them, Mirabel must weigh the stability she clawed together against a second chance that demands she risk everything again. In the end, she chooses truth over safety: she hands her daughter and the shop's keys to a trusted friend, boards the last ferry of the season, and chooses Jonah — not as the person she lost, but as the person they've both become.
about_author: Ulyana Montrose is a former small-town librarian who writes love stories about second chances and the letters we never send. She lives on a windswept island ferry route, where she collects postcards and overheard farewells.

chapters.title: Water-Damaged
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. A storm floods the bookshop basement, and while salvaging stock Mirabel finds an unopened letter addressed to her, postmarked eleven years ago — in Jonah's handwriting. Her daughter, Wren, finds her weeping over it. Emotional beat: the past cracks open the carefully sealed present, and curiosity wars with self-protection.

chapters.title: The Man on the Ferry Dock
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Mirabel and Jonah. Jonah returns to settle his mother's estate and walks into the bookshop to apologize for a letter he assumed was answered with silence. They argue, then agree to read it together — discovering his mother hid it out of loyalty to her own fears. Emotional beat: grief and fury give way to the terrifying realization that they were stolen from each other, not abandoned.

chapters.title: What We Owed Each Other
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, then Mirabel's. Over two weeks they retrace their old haunts while the ferry season's end looms; Wren quietly bonds with Jonah, complicating everything. But Jonah's firm offers him a partnership contingent on returning abroad, and Mirabel, terrified of being left again, pushes him away first. Emotional beat: loyalty to the selves they built apart collides with the truth that they still belong together.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. On departure day, Jonah leaves a letter of his own in the shop — this time hand-delivered, impossible to hide. Mirabel races the ferry schedule, entrusts the shop to her friend, and reaches the dock as the gangway rises. Jonah steps off. Emotional beat: the climax of choice and the resolution of belonging — they choose each other with full knowledge of the price, and the town, and Wren, make room for him.
